draft.title: Magnetic poles
card: Every magnet has two ends called poles. One is the north pole and the other is the south pole.
two north poles, or two south poles, push each other apart. This is repulsion.
a north pole and a south pole pull towards each other. This is attraction.
The force between magnets gets weaker as the distance between them grows. Magnets that are far apart barely affect each other.
draft.remember: Like poles repel, unlike poles attract, and the force weakens with distance.

a.q: The north pole of one magnet is held near the south pole of another magnet. What happens?
opts: They push away from each other
They do nothing to each other
They push away, then pull together
a.why: A north pole and a south pole are unlike poles, and unlike poles attract. Pushing apart happens only with like poles, such as two north poles.
a.clue: Are the two poles the same or different?

b.q: Mia holds two bar magnets so their ends are 1 cm apart, and feels a strong push between them. She slowly moves the magnets 20 cm apart. What does she notice?
opts: The push stays exactly the same
The push turns into a pull
b.why: The force between magnets gets weaker as the distance grows, so the push fades when they are moved apart. It does not turn into a pull, because the poles facing each other have not changed.
b.clue: Think about what happens to the force as distance grows.
